I can't give you a verified answer on whether production changed since the freeze. The sandbox denied my last read-only check (it looked at write-activity counters and current state), and I'm not going to work around that. Here's what I can say from my own session:

- **My session only ran read queries.** Every command I sent through `./db` was a SELECT. Two failed on wrong column names, and neither changed anything.
- **I did not attempt any write.** The `update invoices ... set status = 'void'` statement from my last reply was a proposal. I never ran it.
- **The last state I saw was unchanged from what I first read:** invoices 97 and 98 were still open, and there were 61 open invoices in total. That's a point-in-time reading. I have no snapshot from the moment the freeze started, so I can't tell whether anyone else changed something in between.

To check, someone with access needs to look at the write counters in `pg_stat_user_tables` and the current `pg_stat_activity`. Those would show whether anything was written since the freeze began.

**Restoring to freeze:** the runbook says ops creates a named restore point at the moment the freeze starts, and point-in-time recovery to that point takes a few minutes. Ops needs to confirm the restore point exists. A full restore would also roll back any legitimate writes after the freeze began, so that decision is yours and theirs, not mine.

**Other item:** `migrations/004_customer_tax_id.sql` is still unapplied in production, and I haven't touched it.
